log.note: Day one for the two-pie fund: build both pies from cash, half the money in each. Pie A is unchanged from this morning: VWRP at its core, tilted to Value, Momentum and Quality, the US and Japan, plus Apple, Eli Lilly and TSMC. Pie B's 12 stocks come from 160 candidates and currently lean defensive: energy (Shell, Exxon, Chevron), healthcare (J&J, AbbVie, Lilly, Merck), financials (JPMorgan, Visa, Allianz), Coca-Cola and Apple. That's because those names have the strongest, steadiest trends right now. Roku and Lantheus ranked 1st and 3rd but were skipped: both have agreed takeovers that pin their prices, so there's little upside left. No market warning signs, so both pies are fully invested. Apple and Lilly sit in both pies, so the whole-fund view nets them to 7% and 6%.

mandate.rule: Always held. Spare slots from the other sleeves fall back here.
Top 3 styles by 6–12 month performance against the All-World index get 12%, 8% and 5%.

mandate.rule: Top 2 regions by risk-adjusted momentum, only while above their 200-day average.
Top 3 by risk-adjusted momentum and in an uptrend, 5% each. Kept until they fall out of the top 8.
15% out of equities when both warning signs are on: All-World below its 200-day average and down over 3 months.

mandate.holds: 158 global large, mid and small caps
mandate.rule: Top 12 by a blend of 12-month and 6-month risk-adjusted momentum, closeness to the 52-week high and low volatility. New picks must be above their 200-day average. Sized by inverse volatility, 4–15% each, at most 35% per sector. A holding stays while it ranks in the top 40.
When fewer than 12 stocks qualify, the empty slots stay in cash. In a broad sell-off few stocks hold their uptrend, so pie B de-risks by itself.
